OPEN-QUESTION: THE ONE FINDING WORTH AN OPERATOR DECISION, not a doc typo. PRECEDENT.md:126-129
frames the whole tier ladder as mechanical: "Bindingness is a function of how much adversarial
process a decision survived... Each tier is keyed to a fact a CLI can check by reading the log,
never to an assertion in the record's own text." What publish actually checks is the SHAPE of the
tier_evidence token, not whether the anchoring fact exists. tier_evidence_kind_ok()
(precedent.py:285-294) tests token KIND only; resolution happens later and, per section 5.2, a
dangling tier_evidence entry is a WARNING, never a refusal. Consequence, replayed live:
$ python3 .harness/bin/precedent.py publish --root <scratch> --agent probe --task T-346 \
    --title "tier2 on a phantom P-number" --subject tier2-phantom --tier 2 \
    --tier-evidence P-999 --ratio "binding on everyone, anchored to nothing" --width wide \
    --scope "role:worker everywhere" --revisit-trigger never
  warning: 1 dangling citation token(s): P-999
  published PR-001
  exit=0
$ python3 .harness/bin/precedent.py show --root <scratch> PR-001
  tier: 2  tier_evidence: ['P-999']  status: active
A TIER-2 record - the tier the document itself calls "constitutional... binding on all agents" -
is now live, active, and anchored to a P-number that does not exist and never did. The same holds
at tier 1 (an event:TS token that matches no line in events.jsonl) and tier 3 (a T-NNN with no
task file). Nothing in the code or the document catches it at publish time; only a later
conflicts sweep reports it as a detector-5 dangling citation, after the record has been circulating
as binding.

This is NOT internal contradiction - section 5.2's warn-not-refuse rule is deliberate and
well-argued ("a registry that refused to publish evidence of its own gaps could never record the
exact defect this layer exists to catch"). It is an OVERCLAIM in section 3's framing: the CLI
checks that the record cites something SHAPED like the observable fact, not that the fact is
observable. For tier 4 (persuasive only) that is harmless. For tiers 1-2, where the document says
the record binds everyone, the gap sits exactly where the corpus warning bites - the layer's own
grounding is that author self-declaration about reach measures ~2x random, which is why scope needs
confirmation; an unverifiable tier anchor is the same failure mode moved onto the field that
decides bindingness itself.

WHY THE OBVIOUS FIX IS AVAILABLE AND CHEAP, which is what makes this worth the operator's time
